parameters.excerpt: The `miselect` register implements at least enough bits to support all implemented `miselect` values (corresponding to the implemented extensions that utilize `miselect`/`mireg*` to indirectly access register state).
parameters.reasoning: The spec mandates a minimum width (enough bits for implemented extensions) but allows the implementer to provide more bits up to XLEN. This is a direct design-time choice not controlled by any CSR field.

parameters.excerpt: The `miselect` register may be read-only zero if there are no extensions implemented that utilize it.
parameters.reasoning: The implementation chooses whether miselect is read-only zero (when no extensions use it) or read-write. This controls the mutability of the CSR, a classic NORM_CSR_RW parameter.

parameters.excerpt: The `siselect` register will support the value range 0..0xFFF at a minimum. A future extension may define a value range outside of this minimum range. Only if such an extension is implemented will `siselect` be required to support larger values.
parameters.reasoning: The spec requires at least 12 bits (0..0xFFF) but the implementer may provide more bits (up to XLEN) if they implement extensions that need them. This is a direct implementation choice.
